extracted.intended_audience: Weill Cornell Medicine / Cornell-Ithaca faculty (early-career investigators, assistant professors running independent labs) preparing a nomination for the Pew Biomedical Scholars Program
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation standards for institutional nomination to the Pew Biomedical Scholars Program, specifying eligibility, selection priorities, required application materials, formatting, and budget constraints for early-career biomedical investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and allowable uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget: $75,000 per year for a 4-year period. The amount of the award that may be used for the principal investigator’s salary is limited to $12,500 per year (including benefits) or $50,000 over the duration of the grant. There are no limits on student or postdoctoral salaries. No more than 8% of the total award may be allocated for facilities and administrative charges or indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scope and research types supported
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides funding to early-career investigators of outstanding promise in science relevant to the advancement of human health. This program does not fund public health projects or clinical trials research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong proposals will incorporate particularly creative and pioneering approaches to basic, translational, and applied biomedical research. Candidates whose work is based on biomedical principles but who bring in concepts and theories from more diverse fields are encouraged to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on high-impact, non-incremental research
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas with the potential to produce an unusually high impact are encouraged. Successful applications should not look like typical R01 grant applications with incremental research steps and safe hypotheses supported by existing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew supports truly out-of-the-box, brilliant, early-career science which may accelerate and advance progress to understanding aspects of biomedical research and may not be fundable through other more typical funding mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — project and researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the successful candidates will be based on a detailed description of the work that the applicant proposes to undertake, evaluations of the candidate’s performance, and notable past accomplishments, including honors, awards, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Advisory Committee gives considerable weight to both the project proposal and the researcher, including evidence that the candidate is a successful independent investigator and has the skill set needed to carry out their high-impact proposal. Letters of reference and included essays are critical pieces of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — doctoral degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Must hold a doctorate in biomedical sciences, medicine, or a related field, including engineering or the physical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — appointment and independent lab requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must run an independent lab and hold a full-time appointment at the rank of an assistant professor or equivalent by September 3, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Assistant Professor, Adjunct Assistant Professor, Assistant Professor Research Track, Visiting Professor or Instructor are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — three-year limit on assistant professorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Must not have been appointed as an assistant professor and run an independent lab at any institution prior to June 10, 2023, whether or not such an appointment was on a tenure track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent in clinical internships, residencies, in work toward board certification, or on parental leave does not count as part of this three-year limit. Time limit stands regardless of changing institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application attempt and program overlap restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: May apply to the program a maximum of two times. The same candidate cannot be nominated to both the Pew scholars and Pew-Stewart program in the same year. A candidate can be nominated to Pew scholars one year and Pew-Stewart the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates with dual appointments at affiliated institutions can only be nominated from one institution. If applicants have appointments at more than one eligible nominating institution or affiliate, they may not reapply in a subsequent year from a different nominating entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2027 cycle, one nomination will be invited from each 212 institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cornell, including Weill Cornell Medicine, may submit one nomination. Department Chairs/Division Chiefs/Institute-center Directors may submit no more than one (1) internal nominations from their department/division/institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — 30-line scientific abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: 30-lines scientific abstract explaining the qualifications of the applicant and fit of the project for this funding mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this as the first item in the single PDF in the order listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — nomination letter
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1-2-page nomination letter by the Department Chair/Division Chief/Institute Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must describe the candidate's achievement and why they are deserving of this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — biosketch and support listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's biosketch with complete contact info, education and work experience, publications and awards. The Biosketch must include the nominee's appointment date (month/day/year). List all current research support (internal/start-up and external) and pending support (in an additional page, if needed), including dollar amounts and start/end dates. Include any research overlap with the proposed project of funded awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — 2-page research description
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2-page description of the candidate's proposed research, highlighting particularly creative and risk-taking aspects of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief statement of how receipt of the award would benefit the candidate and why the research is personally significant to them. Any references can be in addition to the two-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — influential publications summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe briefly up to 3 of the most influential publications including information on their significance (1-page max.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, file assembly, naming, and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload the above items in the order listed in one single PDF file using the following naming convention: PI last name-first initial_PewScholars-2027.pdf (Example: Smith-J_PewScholars-2027.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Margins should be at least one inch and font size not less than 12 point. Upload no later than March 30, 2026, at 11:59 pm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission status and conflicts with other funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission: By invitation from the Foundation only. Funding from the NIH, other government sources, and project grants from nonprofit associations do not pose a conflict with the Pew scholars program.
